0.symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and scabby lesions on fruits. Leaf curling and premature drop.
0.organic_treatment: Apply sulfur or copper sprays early in spring. Prune trees to increase airflow and remove fallen leaves promptly.
0.chemical_treatment: Fungicides containing Captan, Mancozeb, or Myclobutanil during bud break and petal fall.
0.prevention: Plant resistant cultivars (e.g., Honeycrisp, Enterprise). Ensure proper tree pruning and sanitize orchard ground.

1.symptoms: Purple flecks expanding into circular lesions with light brown centers ('frogeye' spots) and rotting black fruit with concentric rings.
1.organic_treatment: Remove and burn mummified fruits and dead limbs. Spray bio-fungicide like Bacillus subtilis.
1.chemical_treatment: Captan or Thiophanate-methyl applications from silver tip through harvest intervals.
1.prevention: Prune out dead wood and fire-blight strikes; control insect damage which serves as infection entry points.

2.symptoms: Bright orange or yellow spots on the upper leaf surface with tube-like spore structures on the lower surface.
2.organic_treatment: Apply liquid copper or sulfur sprays before floral bloom. Remove nearby Eastern red cedar galls.
2.chemical_treatment: Apply sterol-inhibiting fungicides such as Myclobutanil or Propiconazole at pink bud stage.
2.prevention: Avoid planting susceptible apple trees within several hundred feet of Juniper/Cedar trees.

3.symptoms: Foliage is vibrant green, firm, and showing robust physiological vigor with no visible blemishes or necrosis.
3.organic_treatment: Maintain balanced organic fertilization, compost topdressing, and regular drip irrigation.
3.prevention: Continue standard seasonal pest scouting and clean orchard maintenance.

4.symptoms: Leaves are glossy, uniform deep green with clean margins and vigorous stem development.
4.organic_treatment: Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5–5.2) using elemental sulfur and organic pine bark mulch.
4.prevention: Maintain acidic soil moisture and monitor for spotted wing drosophila.

5.symptoms: White powdery fungal coating on leaves and young shoots, causing leaf distortion and curling upwards.
5.organic_treatment: Neem oil, potassium bicarbonate spray, or diluted whey/milk solution applied on affected foliage.
5.chemical_treatment: Apply sulfur or quinoxyfen, myclobutanil, or tebuconazole fungicides.
5.prevention: Avoid overhead watering; prune canopy to promote sunshine penetration and low relative humidity.

6.symptoms: Leaves exhibit healthy dark green coloration, no signs of fungal spots or shot-hole lesions.
6.organic_treatment: Standard annual mulching and balanced foliar micronutrient feeding.
6.prevention: Maintain dormant copper spray in winter to prevent bacterial canker.

7.symptoms: Rectangular, tan-to-gray leaf lesions delimited by veins, coalescing to cause extensive foliar blighting.
7.organic_treatment: Crop rotation with non-host legumes; thorough incorporation of crop residue after harvest.
7.chemical_treatment: Foliar fungicides with strobilurin (azoxystrobin) or triazole chemistry applied between V12 and R2 stages.
7.prevention: Plant resistant hybrid maize seed varieties and practice 2-year crop rotation.

8.symptoms: Oval, cinnamon-brown to golden-brown pustules scattered across both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
8.organic_treatment: Ensure adequate spacing and plant early in season to avoid late-season airborne spore peaks.
8.chemical_treatment: Pyraclostrobin or Propiconazole foliar sprays if rust pustules appear before blister stage.
8.prevention: Use certified rust-resistant maize hybrid seeds.

9.symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (1 to 6 inches long) primarily on lower leaves first.
9.organic_treatment: Deep tillage to bury infected stalk debris and ensure wide crop rotation away from continuous corn.
9.chemical_treatment: Triazole or strobilurin fungicides applied at tasseling stage if disease pressure is high.
9.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids (Ht genes) and maintain proper soil potassium levels.

10.symptoms: Leaves are broad, healthy dark emerald green, showing upright turgidity and no lesions.
10.organic_treatment: Optimal nitrogen side-dressing and organic compost application.
10.prevention: Maintain uniform irrigation and soil weed management.

11.symptoms: Small, reddish-brown circular spots on leaves; berries shrivel into hard, black, wrinkled mummies.
11.organic_treatment: Remove and destroy mummified grape clusters and infected canes during winter pruning. Apply copper.
11.chemical_treatment: Mancozeb, Ziram, or Myclobutanil applications from bud break through 4 weeks post-bloom.
11.prevention: Maintain an open vine canopy for fast leaf drying after rain.

12.symptoms: Tiger-stripe patterns of yellow/brown necrosis between veins; dark spots on berries and sudden vine apoplexy.
12.organic_treatment: Trunk renewal; paint pruning wounds with Trichoderma harzianum bio-protectant paste.
12.chemical_treatment: No curative systemic fungicide exists; apply wound-protectant pastes like thiophanate-methyl.
12.prevention: Prune during dry winter periods to minimize wound infection by wood-rotting fungi.

13.symptoms: Irregular dark brown lesions with distinct borders on older leaves, causing defoliation in late summer.
13.organic_treatment: Bordeaux mixture (copper sulfate + lime) spray during post-bloom season.
13.prevention: Ensure good air circulation within the trellis trellis system.

14.symptoms: Lush green foliage with pristine leaves, strong tendril growth, and clean canes.
14.organic_treatment: Balanced soil management, potassium and magnesium foliar feeds.
14.prevention: Routine canopy management and shoot positioning.

15.symptoms: Asymmetric blotchy mottling on leaves, yellow shoots, vein corking, and bitter, lopsided fruit that stays green at base.
15.organic_treatment: Strict biological control of the Asian citrus psyllid vector using Tamarixia radiata parasitoid wasps. Soil nutrition boosts.
15.chemical_treatment: Control psyllid vectors with systemic insecticides (imidacloprid, thiamethoxam). Soil antimicrobial trunk injections where permitted.
15.prevention: Use certified disease-free nursery stock, remove infected trees quickly to prevent grove-wide spread.

16.symptoms: Angular, water-soaked purplish lesions that drop out creating a shot-hole appearance; cracked fruit.
16.organic_treatment: Oxytetracycline or copper sprays at low concentrations to avoid phytotoxicity.
16.chemical_treatment: Copper bactericides applied from dormant stage through petal fall.
16.prevention: Plant resistant peach cultivars and avoid planting in sandy, wind-exposed sites without windbreaks.

17.symptoms: Glossy lanceolate leaves free of spotting, healthy shoot extension, and robust green growth.
17.organic_treatment: Balanced nitrogen management and organic compost mulch.
17.prevention: Maintain dormant copper sprays against peach leaf curl during winter.

18.symptoms: Small, water-soaked circular to irregular lesions turning brown with yellow halos. Severe leaf drop exposing fruit to sunscald.
18.organic_treatment: Copper-based bactericides combined with bio-stimulants; avoid handling wet plants.
18.chemical_treatment: Copper hydroxide mixed with Mancozeb spray program during rainy weather.
18.prevention: Use hot-water treated or certified disease-free seeds; drip irrigate instead of overhead sprinklers.

19.symptoms: Deep emerald foliage, crisp erect leaves, healthy blossoms, and uniform growth.
19.organic_treatment: Seaweed extract foliar spray and calcium-rich bone meal soil feeding.
19.prevention: Maintain even soil moisture to prevent blossom-end rot.

20.symptoms: Dark brown, circular lesions with characteristic concentric rings ('target board' pattern) on older lower leaves.
20.organic_treatment: Copper soaps, Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bio-fungicide, and removing lower diseased foliage.
20.chemical_treatment: Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Azoxystrobin applications starting when canopy closes.
20.prevention: Maintain plant vigor with adequate nitrogen and avoid overhead irrigation late in the afternoon.

21.symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions on leaf tips and stems with white fuzzy fungal growth on the underside during humid weather. Rapid plant collapse.
21.organic_treatment: Immediate copper hydroxide or copper sulfate spray. Destroy heavily infected vines before tuber harvest.
21.chemical_treatment: Systemic fungicides such as Metalaxyl, Dimethomorph, or Cymoxanil applied on weather forecast alert.
21.prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers, eliminate volunteer potatoes, and monitor blighted culms.

22.symptoms: Robust green canopy, turgid leaves, and healthy stem architecture with zero foliar spotting.
22.organic_treatment: Hill plants with rich compost and mulch to protect developing tubers.
22.prevention: Follow a strict 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.

23.symptoms: Compound leaves are vibrant green with serrated margins, free from cane blight or rust spots.
23.organic_treatment: Topdress with aged manure and pine mulch; ensure adequate trellis support.
23.prevention: Prune out spent floricanes after summer fruiting.

24.symptoms: Trifoliate leaves are uniformly green, free from defoliation or frogeye lesions.
24.organic_treatment: Ensure active Rhizobium bacterial inoculation for biological nitrogen fixation.
24.prevention: Scout periodically for soybean aphids and pod borers.

25.symptoms: Talcum-powder like white fungal patches covering both leaf surfaces, leading to leaf yellowing and sun-scorched fruit.
25.organic_treatment: Potassium bicarbonate spray, horticultural neem oils, or sulfur dusting.
25.chemical_treatment: Myclobutanil, Trifloxystrobin, or Boscalid fungicides applied upon first appearance.
25.prevention: Plant resistant squash varieties and allow wide spacing for sunlight penetration.

26.symptoms: Irregular purple to brown blotches covering leaves; tissue between spots turns brown and leaf edges curl up dry.
26.organic_treatment: Remove and compost severely blighted leaves after harvest. Apply liquid copper.
26.chemical_treatment: Captan, Pyraclostrobin, or Cyprodinil fungicides applied in early spring growth.
26.prevention: Renovate strawberry beds annually, avoid high nitrogen fertilizer that promotes excess dense foliage.

27.symptoms: Lush trifoliate leaves with bright serrated margins, strong runner growth, and clean crowns.
27.organic_treatment: Mulch beds with clean straw to elevate fruit and foliage off wet soil.
27.prevention: Maintain drip irrigation and remove runner overcrowding.

28.symptoms: Small, water-soaked dark spots on leaves with yellow halos, coalescing to cause leaf scorch and defoliation.
28.organic_treatment: Copper bactericides mixed with Bacillus subtilis; sterilize pruning shears between plants.
28.chemical_treatment: Copper hydroxide combined with Mancozeb sprays at 7–10 day intervals in warm wet weather.
28.prevention: Use certified seed, water at base of stems, avoid overhead sprinklers.

29.symptoms: Brown to black lesions with concentric rings ('target' shape) developing on lower leaves first, causing lower defoliation.
29.organic_treatment: Prune bottom 12 inches of leaves; apply copper fungicides and mulch heavily to prevent soil splash.
29.chemical_treatment: Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Azoxystrobin applied every 7-14 days.
29.prevention: Stake plants upright, rotate tomatoes with non-solanaceous crops for 3 years.

30.symptoms: Large, dark greasy-looking spots on leaves and stems with white mold on underside in wet weather. Plants can collapse in days.
30.organic_treatment: Liquid copper spray immediately upon disease advisory; pull and destroy infected plants if severe.
30.chemical_treatment: Cymoxanil, Dimethomorph, or Mandipropamid fungicides applied preventatively.
30.prevention: Plant resistant varieties (e.g., Mountain Magic, Defiant), eliminate volunteer potato/tomato plants.

31.symptoms: Pale greenish-yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces and olive-green to brown velvety fungal patches on lower leaf surfaces.
31.organic_treatment: Increase greenhouse ventilation, reduce humidity below 85%, spray bio-fungicide (Bacillus subtilis).
31.chemical_treatment: Chlorothalonil, Copper hydroxide, or Difenoconazole fungicides.
31.prevention: Ensure good spacing and circulation in high tunnels or greenhouses; avoid wetting foliage.

32.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots with dark brown margins and gray centers containing tiny black speck pycnidia.
32.organic_treatment: Remove lower infected leaves, apply organic copper spray, apply straw mulch to block soil-splash spores.
32.chemical_treatment: Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Copper fungicide applications at first appearance.
32.prevention: 3-year crop rotation, stake vines, remove tomato debris at end of season.

33.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling or bronzing on leaves, delicate webbing under leaves, dry brittle appearance.
33.organic_treatment: Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis), spray insecticidal soap, rosemary oil or neem oil.
33.chemical_treatment: Abamectin, Bifenazate, or Spiromesifen miticides applied to undersides of leaves.
33.prevention: Avoid drought stress; spray water to wash dust off plants which discourages mite colonization.

34.symptoms: Pinpoint brown spots expanding into circular lesions with light brown centers and dark concentric rings.
34.organic_treatment: Copper octanoate or biofungicides; prune lower suckers to improve airflow.
34.chemical_treatment: Famoxadone + Cymoxanil or Boscalid + Pyraclostrobin sprays.
34.prevention: Stake plants off ground, control weeds that act as alternate hosts.

35.symptoms: Stunted upright plant growth, leaves curled upward with prominent yellowing (chlorosis) along margins, floral abortion.
35.organic_treatment: Install yellow sticky traps to catch whitefly vectors; spray insecticidal soaps or neem oil. Pull out infected plants.
35.chemical_treatment: Control whiteflies using Imidacloprid, Dinotefuran, or Spirotetramat (virus itself has no chemical cure).
35.prevention: Use TYLCV-resistant tomato cultivars, use fine mesh insect netting, control weeds around field edges.

36.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic pattern on leaves, fern-like leaf distortion (shoestringing), and uneven fruit ripening.
36.organic_treatment: No cure; rogue out and burn infected plants immediately. Wash hands in milk or detergent before handling plants.
36.chemical_treatment: No chemical treatment cures plant viruses.
36.prevention: Plant resistant varieties (look for 'Tm' or 'ToMV' label), disinfect all gardening tools with 20% bleach solution, avoid tobacco use near plants.

37.symptoms: Rich green foliage, turgid leaves, vigorous apical growth, and healthy blossoms with no signs of pest or fungal damage.
37.organic_treatment: Apply calcium nitrate or bone meal to prevent blossom-end rot; mulch base and prune suckers.
37.prevention: Maintain steady drip irrigation and annual crop rotation.
